pool.text: The Adams-Onis Treaty between the United States and Spain defined the Red River.
Mexico declared independence from Spain, and the area was considered part of Coahuila y Tejas.
Texians gained independence from Mexico and formed the Republic of Texas.
A founder planted a stake in the ground on a Trinity River bluff.
A permanent settlement named Dallas was established by returning founder John Neely Bryan.
The Republic of Texas was annexed by the United States.
Highland Park Village opened as the second shopping center in America.
Dallas purchased 36 acres from John Cole's estate to develop Reverchon Park.
Fair Park was built for the Texas Centennial Exposition world's fair.
Originally located in Decatur, Texas, the school moved to Dallas.
El Centro first opened its campus doors and now enrolls over students.
Restaurateur Mariano Martinez invented the frozen margarita machine.
Paul Quinn College moved to Dallas on the campus of Bishop College.
Belo purchased The Dallas Times Herald and closed the paper down.
DART began operating the first light rail system in the state.
HBC was acquired by Univision and became Univision Radio Inc.
AT&T relocated their corporate headquarters to Downtown Dallas.
A facility joined up with Madrid's Prado Museum for a three-year partnership.
UNT at Dallas became the first public university within city limits.
Multiple shots were fired at a Black Lives Matter protest in Downtown Dallas.
